chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: Esvan Mosby, a planned Alabam book and the Mosby brothers
summary: Spikes doubts there is enough to write a book about the Alabam; he mentions a third Mosby brother who was a salesman at the music store.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Hunting for old band photographs and scrapbooks

blocks.x: Esvan told me he's writing a book about Alabam.
I don't see what he could write a book about there.
I don't know. He and Joe Harris--Joe Harris, who writes an entertainment column for newspapers. Uh, they're friends, and they told me they're working together on a book on the Alabam. And...
They must be just gonna write a lot of fiction because there wasn't all that about the Alabam.
Uh, how much younger was Esvan than Curtis? A lot younger?
Well, I imagine he was because, you know, I had ...there's another boy, Mosby, in between there, you know.
Oh, no, I didn't know. I only knew about the two.

Yeah, the one of them was...uh...oh, I can't... he died here. He was...uh, he had one eye. He...oh, I can't think of his name. When Mosby and I went together in the music store, he was our salesman--outside salesman. He went around and sold phonographs and things on the outside.
Was he involved in performing at all?

No. No, I never did hear of him even playing anything but he was a...a...a salesman. After that--after we closed the music store--well, then he got in with a big furniture store and was selling furniture. A salesman--a regular salesman, you know.
